A1.justification: Both PDFs are readable 14-page versions of Playmate, including Appendices A.1 and A.2. Their text, figures, tables, and equations support a complete comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark results on HDTF and the collected dataset in Table 1, CFG ablations in Table 2, and a Gaussian-noise augmentation ablation in Appendix A.2.

after.justification: v2 retains the original benchmark results, quantitative ablations, and qualitative experiments, including the appendix results.

M1.justification: The two-stage framework, motion-decoupled module, audio-conditioned diffusion transformer, emotion controller, and Gaussian-noise augmentation remain unchanged in Section 3 and Appendix A.2.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same training datasets, HDTF and collected-data evaluations, and demonstrations across portrait styles and emotional conditions. No dataset or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Table 1 and the visual comparisons in Figures 4 and 8 retain the same comparators: Hallo, Hallo2, JoyVASA, MEMO, and Sonic.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 retains the same training/test allocation, sample counts, preprocessing, evaluation metrics, and training budgets. The CFG-scale evaluation settings in Table 2 also match.

E4.justification: The adaptive-normalization ablation in Figure 7, CFG sweeps in Table 2, Gaussian-noise ablation in Appendix A.2/Figure 9, and visual case comparisons are unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions report the same point estimates without repeated-run or seed counts, confidence intervals, or significance tests. No uncertainty-reporting practice changes.

E6.justification: All entries in Tables 1 and 2 and all qualitative results match. For example, Playmate's HDTF FID and FVD remain 19.138 and 231.048, respectively; appendix results are also identical.

T1.justification: Equations (1)-(10), including the keypoint transformations, normalization, losses, guidance, and noise augmentation, are mathematically unchanged. Reflow around the early equations introduces no new definition or derivation.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about the two-stage framework, attribute disentanglement, emotion control, and generation performance.

C2.justification: Result interpretations and limitations are unchanged, including the focus on the face region and artifacts associated with extreme head movements, texture sticking, and complex backgrounds.

D1.justification: Implementation details, preprocessing instructions, optimizer, GPU resources, training durations, and guidance scales are unchanged. Both versions retain the same future code-availability statement and appendix augmentation details.

R1.justification: Section 2, citations, and the reference list contain the same works and research positioning, including the relationship to face-vid2vid, LivePortrait, and VASA-1.

P1.justification: v2 adds a dagger to Jiaran Cai's author entry and identifies him as project lead in the footnote. Body wording, terminology, and section order remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The enlarged author footnote accompanies text reflow across pages 1-4 and adjusted equation spacing on page 4; the version/date stamp also changes. Figures and tables are unchanged, and pages 5-14 render identically.

improvement.justification: v2 clarifies the project-lead attribution and makes limited layout adjustments while retaining the same scientific content, evidence, reproducibility information, and limitations, including both appendices. These edits do not materially change the paper's scientific support or readability.
